tests-glamsterdam-devnet@v8.1.0 — bal_builder_request_dequeue.json, variant carry_over_from_contract-deposit, block 1:

JSON blockAccessList hashes to 0xccc45fa3b2aa3b6a62b7cce12cbaecdce7d47dc9dbd355d6ac0abc3f5687fa93
Block RLP blockAccessListHash is 0x79384e5cd0fc52f4df41d86f6631a8307b3776d3c5a741c73edbc4eaa2f20dab
EthereumJS generates a BAL identical to the JSON (compareBAL ✓); only the header/RLP field is wrong
Other five variants in the same file are consistent
Suggested upstream fix: re-export block 1 for that variant so blockAccessListHash, block hash, and RLP match keccak256(JSON BAL).

<@755913785620824175> (or other) and another suggestion for a missing case based on this PR we got https://github.com/ethereumjs/ethereumjs-monorepo/pull/4341 (and also on top of v8.1.0:

---

Title: EIP-7928: fixture for BAL storage slot numeric ordering (mixed minimal-length keys)

Problem: Existing BAL opcode tests only use small same-length slots (0x00–0x03). Clients that sort storage keys by byte-prefix on minimal-length representations instead of numeric (32-byte) order can produce wrong blockAccessListHash without failing any current fixture.

Request: Add a blockchain test where a single account accesses slots 0x02 and 0x0100 in one transaction (SSTORE and/or SLOAD), with fixture asserting the full BAL and blockAccessListHash. Reference ordering: 0x02 before 0x0100.

Repro: compare('0x02', '0x0100') returns +1 with prefix-first compare but should return -1.
